findings.title: Shared drum accent owner initially absent from pad projection and write route
findings.observed_initial: The model read selected voice hits irrespective of CHORD and stored no per-pattern shared accent field. CHORD+pad could enter the ordinary hit route in SEQ/MIX. This did not implement the baseline accent owner promised by the copied source ledger.

source_contract.owner: pat_of(kit)->drum[kit].accent; shared by the eleven voices; absolute ui.spage*16+white index
source_contract.display: B_ENV selects shared accent bits instead of hit[ui.sel[kit]], then applies length/content and playhead inversion. Visible drum MIX kit owns it independently of ui.part.
source_contract.seq_input: SEQ white input calls drum_step(ui.part,w,down) on both edges.
source_contract.mix_input: Drum MIX white input calls drum_step(drum_mix_page(),w,down) on both edges, including LIST/HELP after ASK/HOME/SAVE priorities.
source_contract.part_input: Fresh PART white down only auditions selected sound when key_sounds(); no hidden hit/accent write. A prior SEQ-held step has a separate early release path in PART.
source_contract.down_priority: In drum_step, release handling precedes the ENV check. On ENV down, flip d->accent[s], mark B_ENV used and project dirty, return without creating a new normal hit hold.
source_contract.release_priority: Ordinary captured hit release can delete only matching same-step/kit/voice/pattern existing unused short tap (<300ms); an accent press itself creates no normal hold. Do not repurpose every PART release as an accent write.
